newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks rise to fresh closing record.
newsitem.headline: French stocks rise to fresh closing record.

text.p: French stocks, propelled by a stronger dollar which is expected to boost the French economy, rose on Wednesday to a fresh record closing.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index finished up 32.58 points, or 1.35 percent, at an all-time closing high of 2,442.46, undaunted by a weaker opening on Wall Street.
The index also set an intra-day high of 2,450.34 points.
The CAC-40 January futures contract rose 28 points to 2,4446.
Volume was a heavy nine billion francs.
"The dollar's fabulous," a trader said. "The bond market is holding up nicely. The money just keeps flowing in."

The dollar hit a high of 5.5453 francs on Wednesday, bringing its gains against the French currency to 10 percent over two months. Economists expect a stronger dollar to spur French exports and investment.
* Dollar stocks were obvious winners. Elf Aquitaine rose 3.68 percent to close at 535 francs. Total rose 3.1 percent to 465 francs.
* Bank BNP surged 9.24 percent after being including in Cheuvreux de Virieu's favoured list of shares.

* Shares in semiconductor group SGS-Thomson Microelectronics slumped 11.97 percent to 379.40 francs after the company reported a drop in fourth-quarter profits and said that a recovery in global semiconductor demand may not occur until 1998.

* Alcatel Alsthom rose 3.66 percent to 472.60 francs on a growing view the share may be undervalued, brokers said. The newspaper Le Monde said Alcatel SEL managing director Roland Mecklinger told German publication Handelsblatt he expects a positive operating result in 1997.

* Euro Disney rose 6.28 percent to 11.00 francs on a rise in 1996/97 first-quarter sales to 1.13 billion francs from 1.01 billion despite the company's reiteration that 1997 remains a challenging year due to rising finance charges.

* Brokerage Detroyat added Paribas, unchanged at 372 francs, and Rhone-Poulenc, up 1.66 percent at 177.40 francs to its stock list. It removed Michelin, up 0.07 percent at 291 francs, and Pinault Printemps, up 1.58 percent at 2,372 francs.
* Axa chairman Claude Bebear said the new Axa-UAP group had no plans to sell its Paribas, BNP stakes.
Axa closed up 0.92 percent at 352.60 francs.
